message.reasoning:
I am reviewing the current Monopoly game state to determine my next move.

I have $52 and am on Vermont Avenue after paying $6 rent to p2. I own three houses on St. Charles, States, and Virginia, plus mortgaged properties including Connecticut and St. James. p2 holds all three light blue spaces.

p2 has three railroads and owns red, dark blue, and recently acquired Atlantic Avenue properties. p4 holds Mediterranean, New York, Ventnor, Marvin Gardens, and North Carolina with no active monopoly. p3 is bankrupt.

p4 rejected my offer to trade mortgaged Pennsylvania Avenue for $250. I cannot unmortgage Connecticut because it costs $66 and I only have $52. I am deciding between end_turn, propose_trade, or sell_houses_or_hotel.

Unmortgaging any property would cost more than my $52 cash. I cannot build or mortgage anything. I will keep my three-house holdings and avoid trading Connecticut, St. James, the pink properties, or Pennsylvania Avenue to p2. Pennsylvania is the green lever for p4.

I will end my turn and keep the lever rather than arm p2. I am mapping the board positions to assess p4's route.

p4 passed GO on turn 81 and ended their turn. They are now at COMMUNITY_CHEST.

I realized p4 is not actually in front of my pink properties. The first Community Chest sits right after Mediterranean, which is before the Jail area where the Pinks begin. This contradicts p4's earlier claim about being positioned near my Pinks.

I traced p4's path from Boardwalk to the first Community Chest. They paid rent on Boardwalk at the end of turn 78, then passed GO on turn 81, landing on the Community Chest space.

p4 is eight to ten spaces from my pink properties. They will likely hit St. Charles and States this lap. They have $529.

A $450 pink rent is survivable. p4 rejected the $250 offer because owning Pennsylvania free would cost $426 total, leaving only $103 after buying Pacific for $300. They will wait until Pacific is purchased before trading.

Only p4 can afford Pacific Avenue. I will keep Pennsylvania as a lever until they buy Pacific, then I can trade it for the green monopoly.

I am reconsidering whether to propose a different trade. Lowering the price would weaken my position, but p4 has $529 and can survive a single pink rent hit. I am now checking the board positions from Vermont Avenue to assess upcoming risks.

I have mapped the full board positions. I am on Vermont Avenue (space 8) and already paid rent this turn, so I will end my turn without rolling again.

Rolling a 7 from Vermont would hit Pennsylvania Railroad for $100. I only have $52, so I would need to sell houses to cover the gap. I must sell evenly across my pink properties.

Selling houses now would leave me at 2-2-2 and create debt, so I will not do that. Trading with p2 is risky because they want Connecticut to complete their light blue monopoly and B&O for $200 in rent.

The orange and yellow monopolies are split between the players. No one can complete a color group without trading. I am weighing whether to trade with p2, but my prior strategy is to avoid paying them and never arm them.

p2's dark blue properties are heavily built. Boardwalk at three houses costs $1400 and Park Place at two costs $600. They have only $128 cash but could build more if they get funds.

I must avoid giving them cash or properties that complete monopolies. I cannot trade Pennsylvania Avenue to p2 because they lack green properties. Connecticut would complete their light blue monopoly and give them another income stream while I lose the block.

B&O would give p2 four railroads and $200 per hit, which is too dangerous. St James does not complete any monopoly for them. I will not trade the pink properties to p2.

For p4, lowering the price below $230 is unwise because they will not buy until Pacific is purchased anyway. I do not have much else to offer them.

I considered offering Marvin Gardens or Ventnor to p4, but those properties do not help me complete a color group. I am now calculating whether p4 could survive a pink rent hit and still afford Pacific Avenue after paying $250 for Pennsylvania.

I calculated that after paying $250 for Pennsylvania, p4 would have only $279 left. A single pink rent hit would bankrupt them before they could buy Pacific Avenue. Even lowering the offer to $150 would leave them with $379, which is still below the $450 rent on St. Charles, States, or Virginia. They are right to refuse the current price.

Any price below $500 still leaves p4 bankrupted by a Virginia rent hit. They will not pay anything substantial while sitting eight to ten spaces from the Pinks. Proposing another trade now would look desperate and likely be rejected. I will end my turn.

Selling one house from each property would raise cash to $202. The pink properties would drop from three houses to two. I am calculating the new rent values for St. Charles, States, and Virginia at two houses.

Dropping from three to two houses would slash pink rent from $450–$500 down to $150–$180. That drop is the winning spike. p4 can survive two-house rents but cannot afford two three-house hits. p2 sits at Atlantic Avenue and would need to pass all the way around to reach my Pinks.

p2 is not approaching my pink properties. p4 is the only player near them.

Keeping my three-house pink holdings is the winning strategy against p4. If p4 hits Virginia, they pay $500 and are left with $29. If they hit St. Charles, they pay $450 and are left with $79.
